item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem: Samantha drops a stone onto each of these targets. The stone has the best chance of landing on a shaded space in which target?
item.figure_description:
Four hexagonal targets labeled A, B, C, and D, each shaped as a regular hexagon with horizontal top and bottom edges:
- Target A: Divided into 6 congruent equilateral triangles by three lines through the center connecting opposite vertices (a horizontal line and two diagonals). Two triangular regions are shaded: the top triangle (base on the top edge) and the bottom triangle (base on the bottom edge).
- Target B: Divided into 6 congruent equilateral triangles in the same way as Target A. Three alternating triangular regions are shaded: the top triangle, the bottom-left triangle, and the bottom-right triangle.
- Target C: Divided by a vertical line connecting the midpoints of the top and bottom edges, a horizontal line connecting the leftmost and rightmost vertices, and diagonals connecting opposite vertices. Three regions are shaded: a 30° sector in the top-right (between the vertical line and the diagonal to the top-right vertex), a 60° sector in the top-left (between the diagonal to the top-left vertex and the horizontal line), and a 30° sector in the bottom-right (between the vertical line and the diagonal to the bottom-right vertex).
- Target D: Divided in the same way as Target C. Three regions are shaded: a 30° sector in the top-right (between the vertical line and the diagonal to the top-right vertex), a 60° sector in the bottom-right (between the horizontal line and the diagonal to the bottom-right vertex), and a 60° sector in the bottom-left (between the horizontal line and the diagonal to the bottom-left vertex).
item.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
There is only one red marble in each of these bags.

[Image: Three bags of marbles]

Without looking in the bags, you are to pick a marble out of one of the bags. Which bag would give you the greatest chance of picking the red marble?

options.label: D
options.text: All bags would give the same chance.

reference_items.figure_description:
Three drawstring bags of increasing size, each tied with a ribbon near the top, with faint curved outlines inside representing marbles:
- The smallest bag is on the left, labeled "10 Marbles".
- The medium-sized bag is in the middle, labeled "100 Marbles".
- The largest bag is on the right, labeled "1,000 Marbles".

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem: In which figure are one-half of the dots black?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four square boxes labeled A, B, C, and D, each containing black (filled) and white (open) circles:
- Option A: Contains 4 circles in a 2 by 2 arrangement. Top row: 1 black circle, 1 white circle. Bottom row: 2 white circles.
- Option B: Contains 6 circles in 2 rows of 3. Top row: white, black, white. Bottom row: black, black, white.
- Option C: Contains 3 circles. Top row: white on the left, black on the right. Bottom row: black on the left.
- Option D: Contains 5 circles arranged in an X pattern like the five dots on a die. Top-left is black, top-right is white, center is white, bottom-left is white, and bottom-right is black.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
In this diagram, 2 out of every 3 squares are shaded.

[Image: A rectangle divided into 6 squares]

Which diagram has 3 out of every 4 squares shaded?
reference_items.figure_description:
The stem includes a diagram of a rectangle divided into 2 rows of 3 equal squares (6 squares total). The 4 squares in the first two columns are shaded grey, and the 2 squares in the third column are unshaded (white).

The response options show four diagrams composed of squares:
- Option A: A horizontal row of 3 equal squares, all 3 shaded grey.
- Option B: A horizontal row of 4 equal squares; the first 3 squares are unshaded and the 4th square is shaded grey.
- Option C: A vertical rectangle divided into 4 rows of 2 equal squares (8 squares total). The top 6 squares (3 rows) are shaded grey, and the bottom 2 squares (1 row) are unshaded.
- Option D: A horizontal row of 6 equal squares; the first 3 squares are shaded grey and the last 3 squares are unshaded.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.figure_description:
A square grid containing six outlined shapes labeled A through F:
- Shape A: A square measuring 3 units by 3 units.
- Shape B: An irregular stepped polygon with horizontal and vertical edges of varying lengths (not 4 sides, sides of different lengths).
- Shape C: A vertical rectangle measuring 2 units wide and 5 units tall.
- Shape D: A symmetrical 12-sided cross (plus sign) shape composed of five 2-by-2 square sections; every side is 2 units long.
- Shape E: An isosceles trapezoid with a horizontal top base of 4 units, a horizontal bottom base of 6 units, and a height of 4 units.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Three arrangements of 3 tiles labeled Rita, Ina, and Lana]

Rita, Ina, and Lana take turns arranging 3 tiles. Each arranges the tiles in a different shape as shown above. Which of the following is true about the area of the shapes?

options.label: A
options.text: Rita’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: B
options.text: Ina’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: C
options.text: Lana’s shape has a greater area than the others.

options.label: D
options.text: All of the shapes have the same area.

reference_items.figure_description:
Three arrangements of three tiles each, labeled "Rita", "Ina", and "Lana":
- Rita: Two squares are placed side by side horizontally, sharing a vertical edge. A triangle sits on top of the left square, with its base along the top edge of that square and its apex pointing upward.
- Ina: A square sits at the top with horizontal top and bottom edges. Attached below it is a triangle sharing the square's bottom horizontal edge and pointing downward. Attached to the lower-right edge of the triangle is a second square, tilted diagonally downward and to the right.
- Lana: Two squares are placed side by side horizontally, sharing a vertical edge. Attached to the right vertical edge of the right square is a triangle pointing to the right.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

options.text: [Image: 6 squares arranged in two offset rows of 3]

Each figure represents a fraction.

- Figure 1: A rectangle divided vertically into 4 equal strips; the 3 strips on the left are shaded gray, and the 1 strip on the right is unshaded white.
- Figure 2: A rectangle divided into a grid of 2 rows and 4 columns (8 equal parts); the 2 parts in the first column on the left are unshaded white, and the 6 parts in the other 3 columns are shaded gray.
- Figure 3: A rectangle divided vertically into 3 equal strips; the 2 strips on the left are shaded gray, and the 1 strip on the right is unshaded white.
- Figure 4: A rectangle divided into a grid of 2 rows and 2 columns (4 equal parts); the 2 parts in the left column are unshaded white, and the 2 parts in the right column are shaded gray.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
